full_judgment:
2. Short facts giving rise to the suit are these. The predecessor-in-interest of defendant  Nos. 1 to 4, M.A. Naser took a loan of Tk. 40,000/- from the House Building Finance Corporation, briefly HBFC, for construction of a house upon certain land at Road No. 53, Block No. NW(J), Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka which was allotted to him accordingly a house was built thereon. The loan was not, however, repaid. HBFC, therefore, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 88 of 1976 under Article 27 of P.O. No. 7 of 1973 before the District Judge, Dhaka, with a prayed for recovery of its outstanding dues amounting to Tk. 59,630/-. The proceeding ended in an exparte decree against M.A. Naser on 27 September 1977. The decree holder put the decree into execution in Money Execution Case No. 7 of 1978 in which the said house was sold in auction and purchased by the plaintiff for a sum of Tk. 34,62,500/-. After having obtained the sale certificate the auction purchaser applied to the executing court for possession. In the meantime the judgment debtor died and the defendants made an application for substitution of their names in the execution case, but the prayer was refused. The defendants then filed Title Suit no. 555 of 1985 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for an appropriate relief. The suit was subsequently transferred to the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and registered as Title Suit No. 269 of 1987. As the suit was dismissed the defendants preferred First Appeal No. 46 of 1988 to the High Court Division. The appeal was dismissed with an observation that the defendants as legal heirs of M.A. Naser would be entitled to receive the sale proceeds after payment of the legal dues to HBFC. They were also directed to quit the house in question within 3 months. Against the said judgment, the defendants filed Civil Appeal No. 68 of 1989 to the Appellate Division. It was dismissed on 15 March 1989 with a direction to the defendants to vacate the house within 1 month. Without complying with the said direction the defendants approached the executing court with a petition which was rejected on 10th October 1990. The defendants went up in revision. Civil Revision No. 2589 of 1990 but lost, Later on they filed a petition before the Appellate Division seeking leave to appeal from the order of the High Court Division. Ultimately it was dismissed as not pressed. 

 3. In this back drop the plaintiff brought the instant suit on or 22 April 1991 praying for  recovery of a sum of Tk. 18,00,000/- by way of compensation on account of mental anxiety loss of sleep, loss of earnings by way of rents damage to reputation litigation expenses etc. He alleged that he was a bonafide purchaser of the suit property for value but that the defendants had obstructed him to take delivery of possession thereof by filing frivolous and vexatious cases. 

 7. Mr. M.A. Wahhab Mia, the learned counsel for the plaintiff-petitioner submits that on the facts and in the circumstances of the case the learned Judges of The High Court Division were wrong in cat holding that the plaintiff was entitled on the damage claimed in the suit. 

 9. In an action based on malicious abuse of civil processes like the present one, it is obligatory on the part of the plaintiff to allege and proved malice and also that the previous proceedings were undertaken by the defendant without reasonable and probable cause, apart from showing that those terminated in his favour. We, therefore, find no ground for interference in this case.
